quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated when their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is ______.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with other activities.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.explanation: Never allow a drunk friend to ride. Instead, arrange safe transportation, distract them with other activities, keep them until they are sober, and ask other friends to help stop them from riding impaired.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Don't use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, use turn signals to show your intentions, stay visible, keep distance between you and other vehicles, look ahead for hazards, and be ready to react to changing conditions.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.explanation: Ride safely at night by slowing down, using your high beam headlight when safe, and increasing your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead for clues about the road.

questions.question: To reduce your crash risk, you should:

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to avoid obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid obstacles.
questions.explanation: Stay visible, use turn signals and brake lights properly, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, scan the road ahead and behind, and always be prepared to avoid hazards.

questions.question: How do most headache, cold, and hay fever medications affect your body?

options.text: They make it hard to focus.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies cause drowsiness and can impair your ability to ride safely. Know how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: Where is the throttle located on most motorcycles?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before riding.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must have all of these traits, except:

options.text: Be too tight for glasses to fit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight for glasses to fit.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield is scratch-free, protects against impact, allows clear side views, fastens securely, lets air through to prevent fogging, and has room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet helps other drivers see you. Use it both day and night.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down both your physical and mental abilities.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe by keeping you out of blind spots, helping you see better, helping you avoid hazards, and giving you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers do not try to share your lane.

questions.question: A helmet will not give the best protection if:

options.text: It is certified by the DOT.

questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT and state standards and fit snugly to protect you. Inspect it for damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Use your mirrors at a stopped intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
See if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors for cars coming up behind you. Drivers may not see you in time, so be ready to react.

questions.question: You should keep more space between you and other vehicles when:
questions.explanation: Keep a two-second distance normally. Increase this distance when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous by making them tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider discourage other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers.
By riding in the center of the lane.
By riding on the left side of the lane.
By riding in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves no space on either side of your motorcycle. This prevents other drivers from trying to share the lane with you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in other positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch over them.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster may increase danger by making them tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams around other vehicles.

questions.question: Where should you ride to see better before passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic see you.

questions.question: A person drank 8 alcoholic drinks 4 hours ago. The body gets rid of about 1 drink per hour. How many drinks likely remain?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. The person drank 8 drinks and 4 hours have passed, so about 4 drinks remain in their body.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To lean a motorcycle for a turn, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
